info.title: Rudy OpenTypeless Managed Service
info.description: Pre-launch contract for the optional paid service. The local/BYOK desktop remains fully usable without this API. No production service is implied.

servers.description: Replace only with a Rudy-owned HTTPS origin

parameters.name: callbackURL
parameters.description: Desktop callback created by the client, shaped as https://<configured-api-origin>/auth/callback?desktop=<client-state>&code_challenge=<base64url-sha256>&code_challenge_method=S256. Never accept an arbitrary redirect origin or PKCE method.

302.description: Redirect to the identity provider after validating callbackURL and persisting a short-lived, one-time OAuth transaction bound to the client state and S256 PKCE challenge. On success, redirect to the registered application deep link with only code and state; never put a bearer token in a URL.

get.description: Starts browser OAuth for the desktop. The service must parse callbackURL as a URL, require the exact configured HTTPS API origin and /auth/callback path, reject credentials/fragments, require exactly desktop, code_challenge, and code_challenge_method=S256 query parameters, validate base64url state and challenge shapes, and bind them to a short-lived one-time OAuth transaction before redirecting.

200.description: A newly issued revocable desktop session bearer. Return only after atomically consuming the authorization code and verifying S256(codeVerifier) against its stored challenge.

post.description: Exchanges a short-lived, one-time desktop authorization code. The service must hash codeVerifier with SHA-256, compare it in constant time with the stored S256 challenge, atomically consume the code before issuing a session, rate-limit attempts, return Cache-Control: no-store, and never log the code, verifier, or token. Codes expire within five minutes and failed or replayed codes return a content-free stable error.

204.description: Password changed and other sessions revoked as configured
Password credential created after recent authentication

200.description: JSON text result or OpenAI-compatible server-sent event stream

post.description: Enforces the BackupSnapshot schema and x-backup-policy limits before any snapshot is stored. Rejected bodies and payload content are never logged.

200.description: Optional curated packs; local scenes do not depend on this

delete.description: Requires recent authentication or step-up verification. Revokes sessions immediately and returns a trackable deletion receipt.

bearerAuth.description: Revocable desktop session token; never stored in WebView persistence or logs

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Unique per side-effecting intent; replay returns the original result

Session.description: Authenticated session; native clients may receive set-auth-token

set-auth-token.description: Move immediately to the OS credential vault

schema.description: Return a short-lived HTTPS URL on the exact configured managed API origin. That managed endpoint may redirect in the external browser to the billing provider; the desktop WebView never opens an arbitrary provider origin directly.

url.description: HTTPS URL with no user-info credentials or fragment and an origin exactly equal to the configured managed API origin.

BackupSnapshot.description: Current desktop backup snapshot. The service validates this exact allow-list before storage; it never stores rejected payloads or logs payload content.

x-backup-policy.propertyNameNormalization: Lowercase each property name, remove non-alphanumeric characters, and reject if the result contains a listed token.

message.description: Safe user-facing text without upstream response bodies or user content

BackupDownload.description: Latest snapshot. version and createdAt may be absent only for a legacy pre-versioning snapshot during migration.

BackupHotkeyConfig.x-scalar-binding-consistency: dictation, ask, and translate must equal the first element of their corresponding Bindings array, or null only when that array is empty.

BackupSettings.description: Portable preferences only. Provider selection, endpoint routing, models, resource IDs, and BYOK credentials are device-local and are never uploaded, returned, or restored.
